subject: Day 10: back-to-birth-weight check; cord stump may detach
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 10. Most term infants reach or pass birth weight between today and day 14. If the pediatrician has not yet confirmed weight regain, call today. The cord stump commonly detaches between now and day 15, and the mother's lochia is light pink-brown and tapering.

Action items
- If Avi has not been weighed since hospital discharge, call the pediatrician today to confirm the weight-regain trajectory. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Keep the cord stump dry and the diaper folded below it; sponge baths only until it detaches and the base looks dry. AAP HealthyChildren on cord care: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/bathing-skin-care/Pages/Umbilical-Cord-Care.aspx
- If the SSN has arrived, open the 529 plan this week — front-loading the early years compounds the most. 529 plan overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/529_plan
- Confirm Avi is enrolled on a health-insurance plan; the 30-day qualifying-life-event window is closing. Healthcare.gov on qualifying life events: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/
- Continue the feeding log — you will hand it to the pediatrician at the 1-month visit.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cord stump dries and detaches between days 5-15; a small spot of blood when it falls off is normal.
- [low concern] Baby acne peaking and starting to resolve; mother's lochia light pink-brown.
- [monitor] Cord still attached and looks wet or smells slightly off — mention it at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] Pus, foul smell, or redness extending more than 1 cm around the cord. Yellow tinge on the legs or below. Weight still below birth weight. Mother's bleeding suddenly heavier or passing large clots.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Accumulate 10-15 minutes of tummy time across short bouts, on your chest at a slight incline if floor time fatigues him. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Hold a high-contrast card 8-12 inches from his face and move it slowly side to side to exercise visual tracking.
- Narrate one ordinary task in full sentences during an awake-alert window — diaper change, bottle prep, dishwashing.
- Lay him skin-to-skin on your chest after a feed; it supports thermoregulation and settles both of you.

Upcoming
- Day 5-15: cord stump detaches.
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt; expect a 24-48 hour feeding-frequency uptick.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens; first social smiles begin.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete

- Reacts to loud sounds (startle, blink, stillness)
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Confirms intact hearing response. Universal newborn hearing screen catches most cases but daily observation matters.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-loud-sound/complete

- Brings hands within range of eyes and mouth
  AAP window: day 0-45
  What to look for: Early body awareness. Not yet purposeful — looks like accidental discovery.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brings-hands-near-face/complete
